revision: 1. Preserve the exact 8×8 starting position and all 32 classic glyphs, but normalize every piece to one optical box, baseline, and shadow strategy; give white and black armies unmistakably different fill/outline values that remain legible on both square colors. Increase rank/file coordinate contrast and size consistently along the board edges. 2. Rebuild the side panel's vertical flow without changing its content: title/context → White to move → compact bounded move-history table with readable White/Black headers and an intentional empty-state row → controls directly beneath. Remove the large dead gap. 3. Keep New Match primary, make Undo and Flip secondary, and unify all buttons, dividers, frame rails, and gold accents under the board's restrained modern-club material system; simplify the nested wooden frame to an outer rail and inner bevel related to panel stroke scale. 4. Add distinctiveness through refined bespoke piece silhouettes, subtle coordinate ornament, and future turn/last-move emphasis, not decorative changes to every square.
conflicts: Classical legibility demands conventional piece recognition, while distinctiveness asks for bespoke silhouettes; refine shared classic forms rather than inventing unfamiliar symbols.
The empty move history is truthful at game start, but its large blank region breaks hierarchy; use a compact intentional empty state without fabricating played moves.
A bold primary button aids action hierarchy, but its flat bright gold breaks the material system; retain dominance using the same restrained gold and surface treatment.
rationale: I weighted board-state readability and continuous game-control flow first, limiting originality to crafted club details that do not compromise chess recognition.
audit_note: Central moderation authored from the task brief, shared r0 screenshot, and all four shared axis critiques only. No FUSED or MAD outputs, generated revisions, HTML variants, or scores were inspected.
